context.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid healthcare IT platform designed to manage patient admissions, EMRs, scheduling, and billing. It provides high availability, secure operations, and regulatory compliance for medium-sized hospitals and clinics.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators, Patients.
- **External Systems**: Lab & Imaging Systems, Insurance Clearinghouses, Identity Provider (IdP), Patient Portal / Mobile App.
- **Core Containers**: Unified API Gateway, EMR Microservice, Scheduling Service, Billing Service, Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise).
- **Infrastructure**: On-premises Kubernetes (`on-prem-k8s`), AWS (`eu-central-1`), IPsec VPN.

## Relationships
- **Patient Portal to API Gateway**: HTTPS / REST and WebSocket via OIDC/OAuth 2.0.
- **Clinic System to Lab & Imaging Systems**: HL7 FHIR over HTTPS (REST/JSON) with W3C trace contexts.
- **Clinic System to Insurance Clearinghouses**: Secure EDI / HTTPS APIs with circuit breakers.
- **Clinic System to Identity Provider**: OIDC/SAML 2.0 over HTTPS for multi-factor authentication (MFA).
- **Hybrid Boundary (`on-prem-k8s` to `eu-central-1`)**: Encrypted IPsec site-to-site VPN and mutual TLS (mTLS).

## Technology Stack
- **Compute & Orchestration**: Kubernetes (`on-prem-k8s`) and AWS (`eu-central-1`) for active-active hybrid architecture.
- **Security & Identity**: Keycloak or Azure AD for IdP; HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager for centralized secret management.
- **Data & Caching**: AES-256 encryption at rest; Redis Enterprise for distributed session state and WebSockets; WORM storage tier for audit logs.
- **Networking & Integration**: API Gateway for rate-limiting and JWT validation; TLS 1.3 for transit encryption.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.99% active-active availability across hybrid regions while enforcing HIPAA and GDPR compliance. It leverages isolated trust boundaries, distributed caching, and asynchronous auditing to meet stringent performance and 10-year data retention mandates.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
• The Clinic Management System manages patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics.
• The system ensures high availability, strict HIPAA and GDPR compliance, and 10-year data retention across a hybrid cloud and on-premise topology.

## Key Elements
• Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators, Patients
• Lab & Imaging Systems, Insurance Clearinghouses, Identity Provider (IdP), Patient Portal / Mobile App
• Unified API Gateway (API Gateway, TLS 1.3)
• Patient Registration Microservice (Spring Boot)
• EMR Microservice (Go / gRPC)
• Scheduling Microservice (Spring Boot)
• Billing Microservice (Node.js / Express)
• Async Claims Processing Worker
• Message Broker (Apache Kafka)
• Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise)
• Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (CockroachDB)

## Relationships
• Patient Portal / Mobile App -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST and WebSocket via OIDC/OAuth 2.0)
• Clinic Management System -> Lab & Imaging Systems (HL7 FHIR over HTTPS REST/JSON with W3C trace contexts)
• Clinic Management System -> Insurance Clearinghouses (Secure EDI / HTTPS APIs with circuit breakers)
• Clinic Management System -> Identity Provider (IdP) (OIDC/SAML 2.0 over HTTPS)
• on-prem-k8s -> eu-central-1 (Encrypted IPsec site-to-site VPN and mutual TLS mTLS)

## Technology Stack
• Go / gRPC: Used for EMR Microservice to achieve <1s P95 load performance and internal low-latency transport
• CockroachDB: Selected for distributed SQL storage with Raft consensus to guarantee zero-downtime availability and 10-year data retention
• Apache Kafka: Implements asynchronous messaging for claims processing to prevent blocking HTTP threads
• Redis Enterprise: Provides distributed session state and WebSocket message broker capabilities
• Vault / cert-manager: Manages automated short-lived internal PKI certificate rotation with 24-hour TTL

## Rationale
• This architecture combines a hybrid multi-region cloud deployment with distributed consensus to satisfy 99.99% availability and zero-data-loss requirements.
• Microservice decomposition with strict encryption, WORM audit logging, and data minimization ensures complete HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

Unified API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud healthcare platform designed to handle patient admissions, electronic medical records, appointment scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It ensures high availability (99.99%), strict regulatory compliance (HIPAA and GDPR), and interoperability with external clinical systems.

## Key Elements
- Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators, Patients
- Lab & Imaging Systems, Insurance Clearinghouses, Identity Provider (IdP), Patient Portal / Mobile App
- Unified API Gateway (API Gateway, TLS 1.3)
- Patient Registration Microservice (Spring Boot)
- EMR Microservice (Go / gRPC)
- Scheduling Microservice (Spring Boot)
- Billing Microservice (Node.js / Express)
- Async Claims Processing Worker (Background Worker)
- Message Broker (Apache Kafka)
- Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise)
- Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (CockroachDB)

## Relationships
- Patient Portal / Mobile App -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST and WebSocket via OIDC/OAuth 2.0)
- Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST)
- Unified API Gateway -> Patient Registration Microservice, Scheduling Microservice, Billing Microservice (HTTP / REST)
- Unified API Gateway -> EMR Microservice (gRPC)
- Microservices -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (SQL / TLS)
- Billing Microservice <-> Message Broker <-> Async Claims Processing Worker (Apache Kafka Protocol)
- Clinic Management System -> Lab & Imaging Systems (HL7 FHIR over HTTPS)
- Clinic Management System -> Insurance Clearinghouses (Secure EDI / HTTPS APIs)
- Clinic Management System -> Identity Provider (IdP) (OIDC/SAML 2.0)
- on-prem-k8s -> eu-central-1 (Encrypted IPsec VPN and mTLS)

## Technology Stack
- Unified API Gateway: Kong/Envoy with Lua/Wasm plugins for zero-trust token validation and routing
- Microservices Backend: Spring Boot (Java), Go (gRPC for high-performance EMR), Node.js / Express
- Messaging: Apache Kafka for asynchronous claims processing
- Storage: CockroachDB for distributed SQL storage with Raft consensus and Redis Enterprise for caching/sessions
- Security & Interoperability: TLS 1.3, mTLS via service mesh, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, HL7 FHIR over HTTPS

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture utilizes active-active Kubernetes deployments across on-premises clusters and AWS eu-central-1 to guarantee 99.99% uptime and low-latency clinical access. CockroachDB and Kafka ensure fault-tolerant 10-year data retention and zero-loss asynchronous processing required by healthcare regulations.

Patient Registration Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed for medium-sized hospitals and clinics to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing. It provides high availability, stringent security controls, and strict compliance with HIPAA and GDPR mandates.

## Key Elements
- Front-Desk Receptionists
- Clinicians
- Billing Specialists
- IT/Compliance Administrators
- Patients
- Lab & Imaging Systems
- Insurance Clearinghouses
- Identity Provider (IdP)
- Patient Portal / Mobile App
- Unified API Gateway
- Patient Registration Microservice (Spring Boot)
  - Registration Controller (Spring MVC)
  - Patient Matching Engine (Java / Algorithms)
  - Eligibility Verification Service (Spring Cloud OpenFeign)
  - Eligibility Circuit Breaker Wrapper (Resilience4j)
  - Audit & Compliance Interceptor (Spring AspectJ)
  - Registration Data Repository (Spring Data JPA)
- EMR Microservice (Go / gRPC)
- Scheduling Microservice (Spring Boot)
- Billing Microservice (Node.js / Express)
- Async Claims Processing Worker (Background Worker)
- Message Broker (Apache Kafka)
- Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise)
- Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (CockroachDB)

## Relationships
- Patient Portal / Mobile App -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST and WebSocket via OIDC/OAuth 2.0)
- Front-Desk Receptionists -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST)
- Clinicians -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST)
- Billing Specialists -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST)
- IT/Compliance Administrators -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST)
- Unified API Gateway -> Patient Registration Microservice (HTTP / REST)
- Registration Controller -> Patient Matching Engine (In-Memory Method Call)
- Registration Controller -> Eligibility Circuit Breaker Wrapper (In-Memory Method Call)
- Eligibility Circuit Breaker Wrapper -> Eligibility Verification Service (HTTPS / JSON with Circuit Breaker)
- Registration Controller -> Audit & Compliance Interceptor (AOP / AspectJ)
- Audit & Compliance Interceptor -> Registration Data Repository (JDBC / TLS)
- Registration Controller -> Registration Data Repository (JDBC / TLS)
- Registration Data Repository -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (SQL / TLS)
- Unified API Gateway -> EMR Microservice (gRPC)
- Unified API Gateway -> Scheduling Microservice (HTTP / REST)
- Unified API Gateway -> Billing Microservice (HTTP / REST)
- EMR Microservice -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (SQL / TLS)
- Scheduling Microservice -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (SQL / TLS)
- Billing Microservice -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (SQL / TLS)
- Billing Microservice -> Message Broker (Apache Kafka Protocol)
- Async Claims Processing Worker -> Message Broker (Apache Kafka Protocol)
- Clinic Management System -> Lab & Imaging Systems (HL7 FHIR over HTTPS)
- Clinic Management System -> Insurance Clearinghouses (Secure EDI / HTTPS APIs)
- Clinic Management System -> Identity Provider (IdP) (OIDC/SAML 2.0 over HTTPS)
- on-prem-k8s -> eu-central-1 (Encrypted IPsec site-to-site VPN and mutual TLS)

## Technology Stack
- Spring Boot: Implements Java-based microservices for patient registration and scheduling.
- Go: Powers high-performance EMR microservices via gRPC.
- Node.js / Express: Handles billing microservices and integrations.
- CockroachDB: Provides active-active distributed SQL storage with Raft consensus.
- Apache Kafka: Enables asynchronous, non-blocking claims processing messaging.
- Redis Enterprise: Delivers distributed session caching and message brokering.
- HashiCorp Vault: Secures and manages external API credentials.
- Istio: Enforces mutual TLS (mTLS) and service-to-service security within Kubernetes.

## Rationale
This architecture uses an active-active hybrid cloud model with CockroachDB and resilient microservices to guarantee 99.99% availability and low-latency performance. Strict component isolation, AES-256 encryption, and immutable audit trails ensure full compliance with HIPAA and GDPR mandates.

EMR Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System manages patient admissions, EMRs, scheduling, and billing for healthcare facilities. It delivers high availability, rigorous compliance, and interoperability across hybrid cloud environments.

## Key Elements
- Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators, Patients
- Lab & Imaging Systems, Insurance Clearinghouses, Identity Provider (IdP), Patient Portal / Mobile App
- Unified API Gateway, Patient Registration Microservice, EMR Microservice, Scheduling Microservice, Billing Microservice
- Async Claims Processing Worker, Message Broker (Apache Kafka), Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise), Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (CockroachDB)

## Relationships
- Patient Portal / Mobile App -> Unifiedational API Gateway via HTTPS / REST and WebSocket (OIDC/OAuth 2.0)
- Unified API Gateway -> EMR Microservice via gRPC (TLS 1.3)
- EMR Microservice -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database via SQL / TLS
- Billing Microservice -> Message Broker via Apache Kafka Protocol
- Clinic Management System -> Lab & Imaging Systems via HL7 FHIR over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Go / gRPC: Used for the EMR Microservice to achieve < 1 s P95 screen load performance.
- Spring Boot: Used for Patient Registration and Scheduling microservices for robust enterprise support.
- Node.js / Express: Used for the Billing Microservice for rapid integration development.
- Apache Kafka: Implements asynchronous messaging for claims processing.
- CockroachDB: Distributed SQL database ensuring Raft consensus, zero-downtime availability, and 10-year retention.
- Redis Enterprise: Provides distributed caching and session state.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture combines secure, low-latency microservices with robust distributed data storage to satisfy strict HIPAA, GDPR, and 99.99% availability requirements. It balances clinical workflow speed with enterprise-grade security and interoperability.

Scheduling Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System manages patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It provides secure, high-availability clinical IT infrastructure adhering to HIPAA and GDPR standards across a hybrid cloud environment.

## Key Elements
- Unified API Gateway (API Gateway, TLS 1.3)
- Scheduling Microservice (Spring Boot)
- Appointment Controller [Component, Spring MVC]
- Scheduling Engine [Component, Spring Service]
- Calendar Resource Manager [Component, Spring Service]
- Slot Reservation Manager [Component, Spring Service]
- Scheduling Data Access Repository [Component, Spring Data JPA]
- Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise) (Redis Enterprise)
- Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (CockroachDB)
- Patient Portal / Mobile App [externalSystem, container]

## Relationships
- Unified API Gateway -> Appointment Controller [HTTP / REST via mTLS]
- Appointment Controller -> Scheduling Engine [In-process Java Method Call]
- Scheduling Engine -> Calendar Resource Manager [In-process Java Method Call]
- Scheduling Engine -> Slot Reservation Manager [In-process Java Method Call]
- Slot Reservation Manager -> Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise) [Redis Protocol / TLS]
- Scheduling Engine -> Scheduling Data Access Repository [In-process Java Method Call]
- Scheduling Data Access Repository -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database [SQL / TLS with serializable isolation]

## Technology Stack
- Spring Boot: Framework for building the Scheduling Microservice and its internal Java components.
- Spring MVC: Powers the Appointment Controller for exposing REST endpoints.
- Spring Data JPA: Manages database persistence and transaction boundaries.
- Redis Enterprise: Provides distributed cache storage for ephemeral slot reservation timeouts using TLS and opaque UUIDs.
- CockroachDB: Acts as the Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database to guarantee ACID compliance, serializable isolation for R-02, and 10-year data retention.
- Kubernetes: Orchestrates containers across hybrid regions (`on-prem-k8s` and `eu-central-1`) with Pod Disruption Budgets.

## Rationale
This architecture uses granular internal components and distributed locking with Redis and CockroachDB to strictly enforce appointment clash prevention (R-02) without sacrificing concurrency. Zero-trust mTLS, RBAC/ABAC token validation, and encrypted caching fulfill HIPAA compliance and security mandates while maintaining 99.99% availability.

Billing Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
The Billing Microservice manages clinic financial transactions, invoices, and insurance claim submissions. It processes payments and coordinates clearinghouse integrations to accelerate cash flow and reduce claim rejections.

## Key Elements
* Billing Microservice (Node.js / Express): Parent container processing invoices and claims
* Invoice API Controller (Node.js / Express): Handles HTTP/REST billing requests
* Claims Orchestrator (Node.js / Express): Coordinates asynchronous claim events
* Clearinghouse Integration Adapter (Node.js / Axios): Manages outbound API calls
* Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (CockroachDB): Stores financial records
* Message Broker (Apache Kafka): Handles asynchronous claim messaging
* Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise): Manages session states and rate-limiting
* Insurance Clearinghouses: External claim processing systems

## Relationships
* Invoice API Controller -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database: Reads/writes invoices [SQL / TLS]
* Claims Orchestrator -> Message Broker: Publishes claim events [Apache Kafka Protocol]
* Clearinghouse Integration Adapter -> Insurance Clearinghouses: Submits claims [Secure EDI / HTTPS]
* Invoice API Controller -> Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise): Caches session states [RESP / TLS]

## Technology Stack
* Node.js / Express: Provides lightweight, event-driven runtime for microservice components
* CockroachDB: Guarantees distributed transactional consistency and 10-year data retention
* Apache Kafka: Enables decoupled, non-blocking asynchronous event processing
* Redis Enterprise: Delivers high-performance distributed caching for rate-limiting
* Axios with Circuit Breakers: Ensures resilient outbound HTTP communication

## Rationale
This architecture uses Node.js components for scalable billing workflows while leveraging Kafka and CockroachDB to guarantee 99.99% availability. Strict separation of integration adapters ensures secure, resilient third-party communication meeting HIPAA and GDPR mandates.

## Overview
The Clinic Management System is an enterprise healthcare platform that manages patient registration, scheduling, electronic medical records, and billing. It provides high availability, stringent compliance, and seamless interoperability for medium-sized hospitals and clinics.

## Key Elements
* Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators, Patients

* Unified API Gateway -> Patient Registration, Scheduling, & Billing Microservices (HTTP / REST)

* Redis Enterprise: Provides distributed caching, session state management, and distributed locking.
* Kubernetes: Manages hybrid cloud container orchestration and autoscaling.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.99% high availability through an active-active multi-region hybrid setup backed by a distributed SQL database. It strictly satisfies HIPAA and GDPR compliance mandates using mTLS, field-level encryption, and comprehensive audit trails.

Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is an asynchronous, high-availability healthcare platform designed to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing. It ensures secure clinical workflows and meets stringent 10-year data retention mandates across a hybrid cloud topology.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators, Patients
- **External Systems**: Lab & Imaging Systems, Insurance Clearinghouses, Identity Provider (IdP), Patient Portal / Mobile App
- **Containers**: Unified API Gateway, Patient Registration Microservice, EMR Microservice, Scheduling Microservice, Billing Microservice, Async Claims Processing Worker, Message Broker (Apache Kafka), Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise), Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (CockroachDB)
- **Message Broker Components**: Topic Manager, Access Control & Encryption Manager, Schema Registry, Broker Health & Metrics Exporter, Data Retention & Tiered Storage Manager, In-Transit Data Masking & Tokenization, Broker Audit & Compliance Logger

## Relationships
- Patient Portal / Mobile App -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST and WebSocket via OIDC/OAuth 2.0)
- Front-Desk Receptionists / Clinicians / Billing Specialists / IT/Compliance Administrators -> Unified API Gateway (HTTPS / REST)
- Unified API Gateway -> Microservices (HTTP / REST and gRPC)
- Microservices -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database (SQL / TLS)
- Billing Microservice & EMR Microservice -> Message Broker (Apache Kafka Protocol / mTLS)
- Clinic Management System -> Lab & Imaging Systems (HL7 FHIR over HTTPS)
- Clinic Management System -> Insurance Clearinghouses (Secure EDI / HTTPS APIs)
- Clinic Management System -> Identity Provider (IdP) (OIDC/SAML 2.0 over HTTPS)
- on-prem-k8s -> eu-central-1 (Encrypted IPsec site-to-site VPN and mutual TLS)

## Technology Stack
- **API Gateway**: Unified API Gateway with TLS 1.3 for secure ingress and rate-limiting
- **Microservices**: Spring Boot (Patient Registration, Scheduling), Go / gRPC (EMR), Node.js / Express (Billing)
- **Message Broker**: Apache Kafka with Confluent Schema Registry and Kafka ACLs for asynchronous event-driven processing
- **Database**: CockroachDB (Cloud-Native Distributed SQL) utilizing Raft consensus for zero-downtime availability and 10-year retention
- **Caching & State**: Redis Enterprise for distributed session state and WebSocket messaging
- **Security & Compliance**: AES-256 encryption at rest, mTLS, SASL/SCRAM-512, and in-transit data masking for HIPAA/GDPR compliance

## Rationale
This architecture uses an event-driven Kafka broker combined with a distributed SQL database to decouple heavy integrations and isolate external latency, guaranteeing sub-second EMR load times and 99.99% uptime. The hybrid deployment with strict encryption and audit logging fulfills rigorous healthcare compliance and data retention regulations.

- EMR Microservice -> Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise): RESP / mTLS 1.3 for transient data caching
- Scheduling Microservice -> Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise): RESP / mTLS 1.3 for calendar lock states
- HashiCorp Vault -> Distributed Cache (Redis Enterprise): Automated TLS certificate and AUTH token rotation via API

## Technology Stack
- Redis Enterprise Software: Chosen for active-active CRDT multi-region synchronization supporting high availability and sub-millisecond retrieval.
- Envoy / Redis-Proxy: Selected for intelligent client routing, connection pooling, and TLS termination.
- Redis ACLs: Implemented for strict least-privilege microservice authorization per key namespace.
- AES-256 and Kubernetes Storage Encryption: Applied to AOF persistence volumes for data-at-rest protection.

## Rationale
- This architecture guarantees sub-second EMR performance and 99.99% uptime across hybrid on-prem and cloud regions.
- Enforced mTLS 1.3, Redis ACLs, and tokenized cache handles satisfy rigorous HIPAA and GDPR security constraints.

Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System manages patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It ensures 99.99% availability and HIPAA/GDPR compliance across a hybrid cloud infrastructure.

## Key Elements
- **Front-Desk Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, IT/Compliance Administrators, Patients** [People]
- **Lab & Imaging Systems, Insurance Clearinghouses, Identity Provider (IdP), Patient Portal / Mobile App** [External Systems]
- **Unified API Gateway** (API Gateway, TLS 1.3) [Container]
- **Patient Registration Microservice** (Spring Boot), **EMR Microservice** (Go / gRPC), **Scheduling Microservice** (Spring Boot), **Billing Microservice** (Node.js / Express) [Containers]
- **Async Claims Processing Worker** (Background Worker), **Message Broker** (Apache Kafka), **Distributed Cache** (Redis Enterprise), **Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database** (CockroachDB) [Containers]
- **SQL Layer**, **Distributed Transaction Engine**, **Storage Layer (Raft Consensus & RocksDB)** [Components of CockroachDB]

## Relationships
- **Patient Portal / Mobile App -> Unified API Gateway** (HTTPS / REST and WebSocket via OIDC/OAuth 2.0)
- **Front-Desk / Clinicians / Billing / IT -> Unified API Gateway** (HTTPS / REST)
- **Unified API Gateway -> Patient Registration & Scheduling & Billing Microservices** (HTTP / REST)
- **Unified API Gateway -> EMR Microservice** (gRPC)
- **Microservices -> Cloud-Native Distributed SQL Database** (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TLS 1.3)
- **Billing Microservice -> Message Broker** (Apache Kafka Protocol)
- **Async Claims Processing Worker -> Message Broker** (Apache Kafka Protocol)
- **Clinic Management System -> Lab & Imaging Systems** (HL7 FHIR over HTTPS / REST / JSON with W3C trace contexts)
- **Clinic Management System -> Insurance Clearinghouses** (Secure EDI / HTTPS APIs with circuit breakers)
- **Clinic Management System -> Identity Provider (IdP)** (OIDC/SAML 2.0 over HTTPS)
- **on-prem-k8s -> eu-central-1** (Encrypted IPsec site-to-site VPN and mutual TLS)

## Technology Stack
- **API Layer:** TLS 1.3, JWT validation via Unified API Gateway
- **Backend Services:** Spring Boot, Go (gRPC), Node.js / Express
- **Messaging & Caching:** Apache Kafka for asynchronous processing; Redis Enterprise for distributed sessions
- **Database:** CockroachDB (SQL Layer, Distributed Transaction Engine, RocksDB + Raft Consensus) for distributed ACID compliance
- **Infrastructure & Security:** Kubernetes (`on-prem-k8s`), AWS (`eu-central-1`), AES-256 at rest, mutual TLS (mTLS), PgBouncer for connection pooling

## Rationale
This hybrid cloud architecture ensures zero-downtime 99.99% availability and strict HIPAA/GDPR compliance for critical healthcare operations. Distributed SQL with Raft consensus guarantees data consistency and durability across regions while meeting sub-second EMR performance demands.
